A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RODS research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and hallucination-evaluation results on AFHQv2, FFHQ and 11k-hands, together with ablations and runtime comparisons in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation experiments and adds image-quality and diversity measurements in Table 1.

M1.justification: The curvature detector, SAS/CAS objectives, perturbation approximations and sampling algorithms are retained. Section 4.3's expanded search–descent–update explanation describes steps already present in Algorithm 2.

E1.justification: Both evaluate unconditional generation on AFHQv2, FFHQ and 11k-hands. The added quality measurements use the same dataset and task coverage; conditional, text-to-image and latent-space applications remain future work.

E2.justification: EDM-Euler, EDM-Heun and the 200-step Euler comparator retain their corresponding experimental roles, alongside the SAS/CAS variants. Newly discussed Trust Sampling and Adaptive Attention Modulation are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a substantial evaluation protocol measuring FID, Inception-Var and DreamSim on 1,000 generated samples per dataset. The reported 11k-hands detection threshold changes from 0.005 to 0.014. Figure 4 also corrects the FFHQ radius caption from 1 to 8, matching the value already stated in v1's main text; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 3–5 replace some SAS/CAS outputs in the existing qualitative correction cases, including the middle AFHQv2 example. This modestly revises case evidence. Appendix B's threshold, critical-step, single-versus-multistep and solver-budget analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing generation seed ranges are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added Inception-Var metric measures generation diversity, while the two-rater description documents annotation rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 1 adds quality and diversity results across all three datasets. RODS-CAS has higher FID than both baselines throughout; for FFHQ, the values are 22.73 versus 20.48 for Euler and 19.56 for Heun. Figure 5 replaces the 11k-hands detection matrix, changing detections from 165/169 to 169/175 under a changed threshold, so this is not a same-setting gain. The existing 14.3% hallucination and 26.3% correction results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian-mixture assumptions, continuation and proximal-update theorems, proofs in Appendix A.1, and curvature-index derivation in Appendix A.2 are retained. Added explanatory prose introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion newly claim preservation of generation diversity and comparable image quality. The central continuation interpretation, RODS contribution, and claims of over 70% detection and over 25% correction remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking threshold choice to dataset backgrounds and explaining why directional errors resist smaller sampling steps. It also discusses early versus late intervention effects, imperfect localization, and unvalidated extensions beyond VE-ODE to VP and latent diffusion. The existing conditional-generation limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release URL and documents anonymized pairwise comparisons, rating definitions, two independent raters and consensus resolution in Appendix B.6. v1 already displayed better/same/worse/unclear outcomes, so this establishes fuller documentation rather than necessarily a new annotation experiment.

R1.justification: Five references are added, supporting the new quality metrics and expanded discussion of Trust Sampling and Adaptive Attention Modulation in Appendix C.3. The broader positioning around continuation methods and robust optimization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Selected method explanations, annotation descriptions and conclusion paragraphs are expanded or rewritten, while the section and appendix organization remains intact. The preprint footer changes to a NeurIPS 2025 conference designation.

P2.justification: v2 adds the cross-dataset quality/diversity table, reworks Figures 3–5 and their captions, and relocates several floats. The original hallucination/runtime table remains as Table 2, and the other diagrams and appendix figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added quality measurements, clearer annotation protocol, code-access information and expanded applicability limits improve transparency and evaluability. The gain is limited: Table 1 exposes higher FID for RODS-CAS on every dataset, but the new comparable-quality claim does not adequately discuss that tradeoff or provide uncertainty. The core method, theory and ablation evidence remain substantially unchanged.
